haiku-low.q1: They see the same 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is refused: the transaction rolls back, nothing is written or sent, and the user sees the same generic 200 message.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes from creation (expires_at). It ends sooner if used_at is set, by a successful reset or a newer reset request for the account.
haiku-low.q4: Still live. The rule failure writes nothing, so used_at stays NULL and the same link works until expires_at.
haiku-low.q5: None. The reset deletes all the user's sessions, including the current device. The user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: It retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the error and drops the job. The user is not told and must request a new reset.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory and put in the queued email job and the link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in reset_tokens.
haiku-low.q8: The API hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and finds the reset_tokens row by token_hash. It is valid only if used_at is NULL and expires_at is later than now.
haiku-low.q9: In the reset_tokens table, as the user's rows counted by created_at within the last 60 minutes. Old rows are kept, not deleted, and age out of the window.
haiku-low.q10: In the issuing transaction, before the new row is inserted, every earlier unused link for the account gets used_at set, so it dies.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: used_at is set on the token, password_hash is updated, and the user's sessions are deleted. The confirmation email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The conditional UPDATE sets used_at only where used_at IS NULL and expires_at > now(). The losing submit updates 0 rows, rolls back, and gets the expired-link page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message as everyone: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The fourth request finds 3 or more reset_tokens rows created in the last 60 minutes (live and dead rows both count). The transaction rolls back, nothing is written or sent, and the user gets the same generic 200 message.
sonnet.q3: A link works for 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if a newer link is requested for the account (used_at is set on all earlier unused links), or if it is used in a successful reset. Opening the link does not burn it.
sonnet.q4: The link is unchanged and still live. The form is shown again with the error, nothing is written, and the same link keeps working until its expires_at.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including the device that did the reset. No session is created; the user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries with backoff up to 3 retries. If it still fails, it logs an error and drops the job. The user is not told and has to request again.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token (32 random bytes) in memory. It puts the raw token in the link (https://app/reset?token=<raw>) in the job it enqueues on the email queue. The worker sends that job by email. Only the SHA-256 hash is inserted into Postgres.
sonnet.q8: It looks up the reset_tokens row where token_hash = SHA-256(raw token from the URL). The link is good only if the row exists, used_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now. Otherwise it shows the expired-link page.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. The count is of the account's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes, so old requests age out on their own as their created_at passes 60 minutes.
sonnet.q10: All the account's earlier unused links are killed by setting used_at = now (not deleted). This happens inside the issuing transaction, after the hourly-count check passes and before the new token row is inserted.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token's used_at is set, users.password_hash is updated, and all of the user's sessions rows are deleted. The password-changed email job is queued only after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The token UPDATE sets used_at WHERE id=<row> AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Only the submission that updates 1 row proceeds. The one that updates 0 rows rolls back and gets the expired-link page.
